title: GneissWeb: Preparing High Quality Data for LLMs at Scale
claim: Our dataset yields models that outperform those trained on other leading open datasets and existing models across training budgets and model sizes.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, green 'ours' curve highlighted over baselines
description: Two side-by-side line plots with grid backgrounds. The left plot is for 1.4B-parameter models and the right plot is for 7B-parameter models. Both plot High Signal Eval Score (y-axis) against Number of Tokens (x-axis). Each plot has three dotted curves with markers: GneissWeb in green diamonds, FineWeb-Edu-Score-2 in orange circles, and FineWeb in blue circles. The green curve sits on top at the largest token counts. The left plot also marks existing models as colored crosses with labels: TinyLlama-1.1B in red at top right, Pythia-1.4B in purple, and Cosmo-1.8B in brown. These fall below or near the green curve's endpoint. Each plot has a legend box at lower right. The eye goes first to the green curves rising above the others.
caption: GneissWeb (∼10T tokens) outperforms state-of-the-art open-source datasets with 5T+ tokens. Specifically, we compare average scores on a set of 11 tasks with 18 variants (zero-shot and few-shot) for 1.4B parameter models (left) and 7B parameter models (right), trained on 350B tokens. We also compare with state-of-the-art existing models of roughly 1B parameter size. Models trained on GneissWeb (green) achieve higher performance than the models trained on other datasets (circles) and existing models (crosses).
abstract: Data quantity and quality play a vital role in determining the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs). High-quality data, in particular, can significantly boost the LLM's ability to generalize on a wide range of downstream tasks. Large pre-training datasets for leading LLMs remain inaccessible to the public, whereas many open datasets are small in size (less than 5 trillion tokens), limiting their suitability for training large models. In this paper, we introduce GneissWeb, a large dataset yielding around 10 trillion tokens that caters to the data quality and quantity requirements of training LLMs. Our GneissWeb recipe that produced the dataset consists of sharded exact sub-string deduplication and a judiciously constructed ensemble of quality filters. GneissWeb achieves a favorable trade-off between data quality and quantity, producing models that outperform models trained on state-of-the-art open large datasets (5+ trillion tokens). We show that models trained using GneissWeb dataset outperform those trained on FineWeb-V1.1.0 by 2.73 percentage points in terms of average score computed on a set of 11 commonly used benchmarks (both zero-shot and few-shot) for pre-training dataset evaluation. When the evaluation set is extended to 20 benchmarks (both zero-shot and few-shot), models trained using GneissWeb still achieve a 1.75 percentage points advantage over those trained on FineWeb-V1.1.0.
